conviction_note: There is no earnings event on 2026-08-31: Aimco already filed its Q2 2026 10-Q on 2026-08-07, and since stockholders approved the Plan of Sale and Liquidation on 2026-02-06 the company reports on a liquidation basis with no earnings release, no guidance and no call, so the calendar row is an aggregator's stale estimate rather than a confirmed print.
searched_and_found_nothing: Confirming the 2026-08-31 event exists. EDGAR shows the Q2 2026 10-Q (period 2026-06-30) filed 2026-08-07 (accession 0001193125-26-338545), and the only filings after it are a routine Form 4 and nothing else. There is no 8-K, no press release and no scheduled call pointing at 2026-08-31. https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000922864&type=10-Q&dateb=&owner=include&count=10 (2026-08-30)

Testing whether the baseline's 8-K item 2.02 history still applies. It does not: the last item 2.02 earnings 8-K was 2026-03-02 (FY2025). Both 10-Qs filed since the liquidation vote (2026-05-11 and 2026-08-07) were filed with NO accompanying item 2.02 8-K, i.e. Aimco has stopped issuing earnings releases entirely. The six reaction moves in the baseline are therefore drawn from a reporting regime that no longer exists. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/922864/000119312526085511/aiv-ex99_1.htm (2026-03-02)

Where the aggregated 2026-08-31 date came from. stockanalysis.com simultaneously shows 'Next Earnings Date: August 31, 2026' and 'Last Reported Earnings Date: August 7, 2026' — an estimated placeholder projected off the pre-liquidation cadence, not a company-confirmed date. https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aiv/ (2026-08-30)

NAV-vs-price gap as a possible edge. The Q2 10-Q puts net assets in liquidation attributable to Aimco at $492.980m against 145,236,898 shares outstanding as of 2026-08-05, about $3.39/share versus a $2.55 close — a ~25% discount. This is a fully public figure from a filing three weeks old, and the filing itself flags that liquidation values are presented undiscounted and that distributions may not equal the estimate, so the discount is a time-value and tail-risk judgement the market has already made, not an information gap. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/922864/000119312526338545/aiv-20260630.htm (2026-08-07)

Insider signal. The only recent Form 4 (filed 2026-08-03, SVP/CAO Kellie Dreyer) is a code-F tax withholding of 4,953 shares at $2.69 on vesting — mechanical, not a discretionary sale. No cluster. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/922864/000092286426000030/form4.xml (2026-08-03)

Post-filing catalyst check. No 8-K, no liquidating-distribution declaration and no asset-sale announcement has been filed since 2026-08-07; the last declared distribution was the $1.30/share paid 2026-06-03. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/aimco-declares-a-1-30-per-share-partial-liquidating-distribution-302759413.html (2026-04-30)

Property-level and market-level angles (apartment concession trends, lease-up pages, local permitting) were not pursued: for an entity whose remaining assets are being sold at contracted or offered prices under a 24-month wind-down, operating fundamentals no longer transmit to the share price the way they would for a going-concern REIT, and there is no event on the date in question for them to transmit into.
baseline_tension: The baseline's own weakness points the same way I do: the unusable option chain, the 510 contracts of total open interest and the -67.8% drawdown from the 52-week high are not a thin-liquidity accident but the signature of a liquidating stub whose drawdown is mostly the $1.45 and $1.30 per share liquidating distributions, and whose prior-reaction history was generated under a reporting regime the company abandoned in February 2026.
